name: Propositional Information Density
description: Measures the ratio of concrete semantic propositions (facts, entities, unique claims) to total word count. AI models frequently suffer from 'lexical bloat'—generating verbose, syntactically complex sentences that convey very little actual information.
algorithm: Semantic Proposition vs. Lexical Padding Ratio Calculation
mechanism: Human experts writing on a subject they understand typically exhibit high Information Density. They pack concrete nouns, specific verbs, and unique facts tightly together, minimizing filler words. Large Language Models, however, optimize for fluid, highly probable token sequences rather than factual efficiency. They frequently employ 'lexical padding': using 30 words to state a concept that requires only 8. This manifests as excessive transitional phrases ('It is important to understand that...'), redundant restatements of the premise, and complex grammatical structures wrapped around simple concepts. This algorithm strips away functional vocabulary, stop words, and known transitional templates. It then isolates the core semantic propositions (unique entities, actions, and distinct concepts) and divides them by the total sentence length. If a text consists of long, perfectly grammatical sentences but exhibits an abnormally low ratio of actual, distinct facts (high 'fluff' ratio), it strictly points to the mathematical padding behaviors inherent in autoregressive text generation.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing essays, analytical reports, summaries, and news articles where concise, fact-driven writing is expected.
strengths:
• Excellent at detecting 'AI waffle'—when a model is prompted to meet a length requirement but lacks sufficient factual knowledge, resulting in perfectly grammatical but semantically hollow filler.
• Captures a fundamental difference between human cognitive efficiency and AI probability-smoothing.
• Highly robust against simple synonym-swapping bypassing attempts.
limitations:
• Less effective on casual or inherently verbose human writing, such as philosophical musings, stream-of-consciousness writing, or political speeches, which naturally feature low information density.
• Requires parsing and POS (Part of Speech) tagging, making it slightly more computationally intensive than simple character counting.
• Can misclassify highly concise AI summaries (e.g., 'TL;DR' bullet points) as human if the prompt explicitly constrained the word count.
parameters:
Analysis: Proposition/Entity Extraction & Syntactical Trimming
Metric: Core Semantic Tokens / Total Token Count (per sentence average)
Output: 0-100 Semantic Bloat (Information Dilution) Score
accuracy: High — 80-88% on informative and academic texts. It is a highly reliable indicator of an LLM's tendency to generate 'safe, verbose, and structurally pleasing' filler.

references.title: Shannon, C.E. (1948). A Mathematical Theory of Communication. Bell System Technical Journal.
Mitchell, E. et al. (2023). DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature. ICML.
